title: Terms of Use
description: The rules for using Arcana Diary: adults only, readings for reflection rather than prediction or advice, free limits, accounts, AI text and liability.
lead: These terms are the agreement between you and {operator_name} for using Arcana Diary at arcanadiary.com. Please read them before you use the site. Effective date: {effective_date}.

blocks.heading: Agreeing to these terms
paragraphs: {operator_name}, {operator_address} (“we”, “us”), runs Arcana Diary. By drawing cards, creating an account or otherwise using the site, you agree to these terms and confirm that you have read our privacy policy at /privacy, which explains what happens to your data. If you do not agree, please do not use the site.

blocks.heading: What Arcana Diary is
paragraphs: Arcana Diary offers tarot readings in English and Spanish. You can ask a question, or none, and draw one card, three cards (past, present and where it's heading), a yes or no reading on one or three cards, a love reading, or a card from a card's own page. A free Card of the Day is drawn for each device and stays the same for that local day.

Cards are drawn at random by our server from all 78 Rider–Waite–Smith cards, and each card has an even chance of coming up reversed. An AI model then writes the reading from the meanings in the site's card base. Follow-up questions about the same cards are possible, and with an account you can keep your readings in a diary, mark whether a reading came true and add a private note.

The site also publishes card meanings and guides. These texts are prepared with the help of AI from A. E. Waite's 1911 book and the site's card base, and read by {editor_name}, the editor of Arcana Diary, before publication.

blocks.heading: Adults only
paragraphs: Arcana Diary is open only to people aged 18 and over. By using it, you confirm your age. If we learn that an account belongs to someone younger, we will delete it.

blocks.heading: Readings are for reflection, not prediction or advice
paragraphs: Tarot does not predict the future, and no reading on this site tells you what will or will not take place. A reading is a prompt for thinking on your own circumstances and your next step, offered for reflection and entertainment.

No content on the site is medical, psychological, legal, financial or safety advice, and it does not replace a doctor, therapist, lawyer, financial adviser or the emergency services. The reader does not name dates, does not promise outcomes, does not state as fact what another person thinks, feels or will do (in a question about someone else it reads what the cards mean in such a question, and a yes or no lean there is the lean of the cards, not knowledge about that person), and does not forecast health, court cases or safety. On those topics a yes or no reading gives no verdict. A yes or no answer about money or purchases comes with the reminder that it is not financial advice. Please make important decisions with the help of qualified people and your own judgement, not on the basis of a reading.

blocks.heading: If you are in crisis
paragraphs: If your question suggests that you could be at risk or thinking about hurting yourself, the site shows free helplines instead of a reading. Arcana Diary is not an emergency or counselling service. If you or someone else is in immediate danger, call your local emergency number.

blocks.heading: AI-generated readings
paragraphs: Readings and answers to follow-ups are generated by an AI model, not by a person, and no person reviews them before you see them. Automatic checks look for things the site does not do, such as promises, dates or claims about another person's feelings, and replace such text with the card meanings from the base; a Spanish passage may be rewritten so that it does not assume your gender. Even so, an AI text can be inaccurate, repetitive, oddly worded or unsuitable for your situation. If the reader is unavailable, you get the meanings of your cards from the card base instead.

Your question and the details listed in the privacy policy are sent to our AI provider to write the reading. Do not include names, contact details or other personal information about yourself or anyone else.

blocks.heading: Free readings and limits
paragraphs: Arcana Diary is free to use. Without an account, a device gets {guest_limit} readings a day; with an account, you get {user_limit} a day, counted across all your devices. Your day follows your browser's time zone. The Card of the Day does not count. Each reading includes {followups} free follow-up questions; a further follow-up on the same reading uses one of your readings for the day, and the number of follow-up questions on one reading is capped. If the reader fails, you can try again a limited number of times without using a reading.

To keep the service working for everyone, we limit how many requests one network address can make in a day, may ask your browser to pass an automated check, and may show the card meanings instead of a written reading when the day's AI capacity is used up. We may change these limits; the current numbers are shown on the site.
A paid plan, Plus, is not on sale yet. Joining the Plus waitlist only means that we may write to you when it opens; it does not commit you or us to anything.

blocks.heading: Your account and diary
paragraphs: You can create an account by signing in with a link sent to your e-mail or with Google. An account is for one person. Keep access to your e-mail and Google account secure, because anyone who controls them can sign in as you. A reading made as a guest can be saved to your account within 7 days of being made; after that it is deleted.

The free diary lists your {diary_free} newest readings; older ones stay in your account and in your download. You can delete single entries or your whole account at any time in the account page. Deleting the account is immediate and cannot be undone. We may suspend or close an account that breaks these terms.

blocks.heading: Acceptable use
paragraphs: Use Arcana Diary only for your own personal, non-commercial use and in line with the law. Do not use bots, scripts or other automated means to request readings or copy the site in bulk; do not try to get around the daily limits or the bot check; do not try to make the reader produce harmful, hateful or unlawful text or reveal its instructions; and do not interfere with the security or working of the site.

Do not enter other people's names or private information, and do not use readings or shared reading links to harass, threaten or deceive anyone. Do not present readings from the site as professional advice, and do not resell or offer the service as your own.

blocks.heading: Your content and ours
paragraphs: Your questions and notes remain yours. You allow us to store and process them only to run the service for you, as the privacy policy describes. You are responsible for what you write.

The site's own texts, card base, design and software belong to {operator_name} or their licensors. Quotations from A. E. Waite's The Pictorial Key to the Tarot (1911) and the card pictures, Pamela Colman Smith's drawings scanned from the first printing of 1909, are in the public domain in the United States and in countries where copyright lasts 70 years after the author's death. You may save, print, share and quote your own readings for personal, non-commercial purposes. Readings are generated automatically, so we cannot promise that a text is unique.
A reading's address shows its cards and answer to anyone who has it, but not your question, follow-ups or note. You decide whether to share it.

blocks.heading: Availability and changes to the service
paragraphs: We provide Arcana Diary as it is and as available. We do not guarantee that it will always be online, free of errors or available in your country, and we may change, pause or end any part of it, including the free limits. If we ever close the service, we cannot promise a notice period, so you can download your diary from the account page whenever you like.

blocks.heading: Limits of our liability
paragraphs: As far as the law allows, we are not liable for decisions you make or actions you take on the basis of a reading, for the content of AI-generated text, or for indirect or consequential loss. Because the service is free, as far as the law allows our total liability to you is limited to the amount you have paid us, which is nothing unless a paid plan is introduced.
Nothing in these terms excludes or limits liability that cannot be excluded or limited by law, or takes away rights that consumer protection law gives you where you live.

blocks.heading: Ending your use
paragraphs: You can stop using the site at any time and delete your account in the account page. We may suspend or end your access if you break these terms or use the site in a way that may harm others or the service. The sections on content, liability and governing law continue to apply after that.

blocks.heading: Governing law and disputes
paragraphs: These terms are governed by the laws of {jurisdiction}. Disputes go to the courts of {jurisdiction}, unless the law of the place where you live gives you the right to bring a claim there. Before going to court, please write to {contact_email} so that we can try to resolve the problem with you.

blocks.heading: Changes to these terms
paragraphs: We may update these terms when the service or the law changes. The new version will be posted here with a new effective date. If a change is significant, we will tell account holders by e-mail before it takes effect. If you keep using the site after that date, the new terms apply; if you do not agree with them, you can stop using it and delete your account.
